newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ColMut confident votes favour demutualisation.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ColMut confident votes favour demutualisation.

text.p: Life office Colonial Mutual said it was confident its policyholders would vote in favour of the group's planned demutualisation and listing following a meeting of Australian policyholders on Friday.

Colonial group chairman David Adam said a favourable show of hands on resolutions presented to an extraordinary meeting of policyholders today boded well for the earlier demutualisation vote which was held by way of a ballot.
"I'm confident. If you were going to vote against the scheme you would have voted against (the extraordinary meeting's resolutions)," Adam told reporters after the meeting.

Results of policyholder votes taken at simultaneous meetings in Australia, New Zealand and Fiji woudl not be made public until their announcement to the group's U.K. policy holders at a meeting in London on November 11.
Colonial plans to distribute A$1.3 billion in shares to its 538,000 members worldwide, and raise another A$550 million, as part of its demutualisation and listing.
Following the U.K. meeting, Colonial's remaining legal hurdle would be approval of the scheme at a December 6 court hearing in Australia.
Chief financial officer Paul Batchelor said the group's ordinary shares would list on the Australian Stock Exchange in May or June next year, should all approvals be won.

The group's managing director Peter Smedley noted the integration of Colonial's State Bank unit was progessing and the banking unit was set to deliver a similar results in calendar 1996 to those of a year ago.
State Bank's 1995 net profit was A$105 million.
